{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the sales data
df = pd.read_csv('/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/sales.csv')

# Verify the actual values in customer_segment
print("Actual unique values in customer_segment:", df['customer_segment'].unique())

# The contract said 'LOYAL', but the data shows 'loyal' (lowercase)
# So we must use lowercase 'loyal' in the filter
# Also, verify the status values
print("Actual unique values in status:", df['status'].unique())

# Clean the 'revenue' column: remove commas and convert to float
# First, check for non-numeric entries after cleaning
# Replace commas with empty string
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False)

# Convert to float
revenue_numeric = pd.to_numeric(df['revenue_clean'], errors='coerce')

# Check for any NaN values after conversion
non_numeric_after_clean = revenue_numeric.isna().sum()
print("Number of non-numeric revenue entries after cleaning:", non_numeric_after_clean)

# If any, inspect them
if non_numeric_after_clean > 0:
    print("Non-numeric entries after cleaning:")
    print(df[revenue_numeric.isna()])

# Now, filter for 'loyal' (lowercase) and 'completed'
loyal_completed = df[(df['customer_segment'] == 'loyal') & (df['status'] == 'completed')]

# Compute the mean revenue
mean_revenue = loyal_completed['revenue_clean'].mean()

# Print the result
print("Mean revenue of completed orders from 'loyal' customers:", mean_revenue)
print("Number of completed orders from 'loyal' customers:", len(loyal_completed))"}
